solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Malicious Head of State examines checks that could assess how much benefit one receives

definitions.text: checks that could assess how much benefit one receives

parts.note: mean can mean spiteful or malicious

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of State is taken

parts.note: to examine is to test, giving tests

explanation.surface: A spiteful leader inspects the paperwork that decides who gets welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of State' looks like a political title, but it only supplies the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A British welfare term: an inquiry into income that decides eligibility for state help, spelt out at length by the definition.

clue.text: European chap upset by our charm

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for chap is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a chap is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from Europe is disturbed by the allure of something belonging to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reads as emotional distress, but in a down clue it means turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to captivate them, making them fond, which is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Antelope set to be raised in North America

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the two letters for North America
in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: to set something down is to lay it

explanation.surface: An antelope is about to be bred in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' suggests breeding animals, but in a down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a spiral-horned species of African antelope, so the clue's animal is a broad category containing it.

clue.text: Servant able to polish concealed part of furniture

indicators.note: concealed tells us the answer is tucked away inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A capable butler is asked to buff up some piece of furniture that is out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' looks like a description of the furniture, but it signals the letters hiding in servanT ABLE TO Polish.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat upper surface of a table is one component of a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Unhappily sniff assent with dosh being withdrawn

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things going awry, so the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs as they reluctantly agree, with the cash being taken back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being withdrawn' reads as money being taken away, but it is the definition. 'dosh' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloofness or reserve towards other people is the state of being withdrawn, a close synonym.

clue.text: Creeps after small flies

indicators.note: the word for creeps is placed after the letter for small

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to edge is to creep forward slowly

explanation.surface: Tiny insects crawl along after something small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun: the sedge fly is an insect, a kind of caddis fly, beloved of anglers.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers use the name for caddis flies and the artificial flies tied to imitate them, so the word names insects.

clue.text: Right time to grieve

parts.note: to rue is to regret or lament

explanation.surface: It is the proper moment for mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and correct are synonyms as adjectives, as in a correct or accurate answer.

clue.text: Passing shot at tennis captivating Queen

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the scrambled letters hold the queen's letter inside
shot means ruined or worn out, so the letters of these words are scrambled

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A passing shot is a tennis stroke that beats the net player, here enchanting the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing shot' is a tennis term, but 'Passing' is the definition and 'shot' the anagram signal: TANSIENT from AT TENNIS, with R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting or short-lived is passing, lasting only a brief time.

clue.text: Discover uranium on new planet

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
our own planet is Earth

explanation.surface: A scientist finds uranium on a newly found world.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up or bring to light is to discover, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Talk about a long story!

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for talk is read backwards

parts.note: to gas is to chatter or talk idly

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone telling a tediously drawn-out tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a preposition meaning concerning, but it reverses GAS to SAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A lengthy narrative, originally a Norse heroic tale, is the sense, and a long-winded account generally.

clue.text: Twix and KitKat? Mars banned, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something going wrong, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two chocolate bars are mentioned, then the news that Mars bars have been banned.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars looks like part of the list of chocolate bars, but it is anagram fodder; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Twix and KitKat are trademarked confectionery products, examples of proprietary trade labels.

clue.text: Cheer very quietly, leaving location

parts.note: so can mean very, as in so happy

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for quietly goes out of the word for location

parts.note: a place is a location
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone cheers very softly while departing a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very quietly' looks like a pair (pianissimo), but 'very' gives SO and 'quietly' the P taken from PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to comfort them; the noun means comfort in distress, matching cheer as a noun.

clue.text: They put clothes on chests of drawers

definitions.meaning: people who clothe themselves or others, such as theatre staff who help actors into costume
pieces of furniture with drawers or shelves, used for clothes or for kitchen crockery

explanation.surface: People lay garments on top of bedroom furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one who clothes people and a sideboard or chest of drawers; both senses are standard.

clue.text: One leaves string of invectives with rotten type of compromise

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for one departs from the word for a string of invectives

parts.note: a tirade is a long angry speech, a string of abuse
one is I, the Roman numeral
food that is rotten has gone off

explanation.surface: Someone stops a barrage of abuse and settles for a poor sort of deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A balancing of competing factors, giving up some of one for more of another, is a kind of compromise.

clue.text: Wild animal died after smash against car's instrument panel

indicators.note: after places the animal and the letter for died behind the word for smash

parts.note: to dash something is to smash it, as against rocks
a boar is a wild pig
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A wild pig dies after crashing into the front of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The panel facing the driver holding speedometer and gauges is a vehicle's instrument panel.

clue.text: Italian novelist grabbing hard copy

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so the novelist's name wraps the letter for hard

parts.note: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist, author of The Name of the Rose
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An Italian writer seizes a hardback copy of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard copy' looks like a printout, but it splits into H and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat or imitate is to copy, as a verb meaning reproduce what another says.

clue.text: Doctor lost knee bones!

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor laments a patient's missing knee bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician, but it is a verb meaning alter, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A body's framework is its bones taken together, so the collective noun matches.

clue.text: Work over, returning to drink

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, a set of six balls

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for drink is read backwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: The job is done, so it is back to drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical composition or artistic piece is called a work, the Latin word used in catalogue numbers.

clue.text: Professional lacking heart to bury dog

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, here dropped

parts.note: pro is short for professional
to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: A pro, missing their courage, has to bury their dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog breed that stands still and aims its nose at game, a kind of hunting dog.

clue.text: Something for writers involved with end of book to put up with

parts.note: to be in on something is to be involved with it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it

explanation.surface: Writers caught up in finishing a book need patience.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk stand holding ink bottles and pens is equipment for people writing by hand.

clue.text: Yank with alcohol keeled over — one's tight

indicators.note: in a down clue, keeled over means toppled, so these words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to yank is to pull or drag
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: An American who drank too much fell over, being drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' and 'tight' suggest a drunken American, but Yank is a verb and 'tight' means stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is someone who is tight, meaning stingy with money.

clue.text: Something attached to a sledge? Bolt, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the long narrow blades a sledge slides on
Usain Bolt, the Jamaican sprinter, is an athlete who races on the track

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what is fixed to a sleigh, maybe a metal fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like a fastening attached to the sledge, but it is the sprinter Usain Bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sledge's sliding blade and a person who races on foot, both everyday senses.

clue.text: Model rubs hair and gets spray

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model rubs her hair and gets a squirt of hairspray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a person in a photoshoot, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A small device that sprays paint by compressed air is a type of spray gun.

clue.text: Adore purchasing a good salad plant

indicators.note: purchasing means taking hold of, so the word for adore holds the other letters

parts.note: to adore is to love

explanation.surface: Someone loves buying a nice salad ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchasing' looks like buying, but its old sense of gripping makes it a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This celery-flavoured herb of the parsley family has leaves used in salads.

clue.text: See — tv is rubbish without electric current

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters go around the letter for current
rubbish means worthless, here messing up the letters of these words

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Look: the television is rubbish without power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' turns TV IS into VIST, and 'without' puts it outside I.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on or go and see a person is to pay them a call, the verb meaning.

clue.text: At Territorial Army in time to capture soldiers, showing talent

parts.note: taken as written
TA is the abbreviation for the Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so the soldiers sit within the preceding letters

parts.note: taken as written
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Volunteer troops arrive just in time to seize men, revealing their skill.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplishment or acquired skill is a kind of talent, a fair synonym.

clue.text: Slap following second argument

indicators.note: following says the slap word comes after the letter for second

parts.note: a pat is a light slap

explanation.surface: A slap follows a second quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty quarrel or squabble is a brief argument.

clue.text: Starts to test rules? Our dad put his foot down!

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, taken from the next four words

explanation.surface: Dad lays down the law, testing the house rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put his foot down' is an idiom for being firm, but here it is literal: stepped.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of tread means stepped, which is literally placing one's foot down.

clue.text: Incoming water — desiring it at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor longing for the flood of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the watery surface, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The flood tide coming in raises sea level, so it is water arriving at the shore.
